lines.bright-mid: The figure's upturned eye and tidy umbrella carry an easy good humor, and the yellow outlines of the book feel almost like sunlight on a gray day. It shares your hopeful, relaxed mood.
lines.heavy-charged: Where your mood is stormy, this poster keeps the rain outside the frame entirely, leaving only calm blue and a dry, well-kept book. Think of it as a shelter to step into rather than a mirror.
lines.mid-charged: The wobbly yellow line around the book gives the page edges a little restless shimmer, but the rest of the poster stays composed. It can catch your energy and help it settle.
lines.bright-charged: The playful pairing of the stern black RAIN with the bouncing handwritten line and its yellow dot has real wit. It is gentler than full exuberance, yet it smiles along with you.

lines.heavy-calm: This poster will not sit quietly with a somber mood, but its pale blue sky and wide white slope give you a cool, open space to breathe in. Think of it as a window onto clear winter air rather than a mirror of how you feel.
lines.mid-calm: The two skiers move in matching stride, poles planted at the same angle, and that steady rhythm has an unhurried ease to it. Against the soft blue and white of the hillside, it feels like a long walk with nowhere urgent to be.
lines.bright-calm: Look at the snow-white hill under a powder blue sky, flat and clean as fresh linen. The skiers are cheerful but never frantic, and the gentle palette lets that warmth settle rather than shout.
lines.heavy-mid: If your thoughts feel weighty, these two figures offer a simple counterweight: bundled in deep blue, they lean into the climb together. It is less an answer than a reminder that heavy going can be shared.
lines.mid-mid: There is something reassuringly everyday in the lettering at the bottom, plain capitals stating that they like winter, as if it were the most ordinary fact in the world. The scene matches that tone, two people out doing something good on an ordinary day.
lines.bright-mid: The red mittens with their white stripes and the hats to match bring a warm, hopeful note to all that cold blue. You can almost feel the easy pleasure of a good day outdoors.
lines.heavy-charged: The drama in your mood has no storm here to meet it, but the kicked-up puffs of snow at each boot give your restless energy somewhere to go. It is tension turned into forward motion, a way up the hill instead of down.
lines.mid-charged: Every line pushes forward: the bent knees, the angled poles, the snow spraying from each step. If you are full of energy and alert, this poster moves at your pace.
lines.bright-charged: Bold blue suits, bright red scarves and a woman's white hair flying behind her in the cold air make this pure exuberance. It shares your joy outright, the thrill of a fresh slope and good company.

lines.heavy-calm: This poster will not match your stillness, and it does not try. Its warm yellow ground is more like a lit window on a dark evening, a small, steady warmth you can rest your eyes on while you stay quiet inside.
lines.mid-calm: The green band of lettering across the bottom sits level and unhurried, holding the flower above it like a shelf. If you want an easy, even day, Kenneth Whitley's poster gives you warmth without asking much of you.
lines.bright-calm: Notice how the chrysanthemum's center softens into white tips, like light caught in the petals. It shares your gentle warmth, a bloom at rest on a sunny yellow field.
lines.heavy-mid: When your thoughts feel weighty, this is a counterweight rather than a companion. The spiky orange petals and plain block letters point you toward something simple and close at hand, a flower show at Garfield Park worth walking to.
lines.mid-mid: For an ordinary, steady day, here is an ordinary pleasure made bold: a single flower, a clear invitation, and dark green leaves planted firmly at its base. It keeps things grounded while adding a little color.
lines.bright-mid: The word MUM curls in looping orange script, friendly and a bit playful against the sturdier type around it. That easy, hopeful tone is close to yours, warm without being loud.
lines.heavy-charged: If your mood is stormy, this poster offers a way out more than a mirror. The chrysanthemum bursts outward in jagged rays, so the energy is there, but it lands as color and bloom instead of tension.
lines.mid-charged: Those flaring petals have real push, each orange point shooting away from the center as if the flower can't sit still. Your restless energy has somewhere to go here, and it goes toward something cheerful.
lines.bright-charged: You and this poster are on the same wavelength. The blazing orange flower against saturated yellow feels like a shout of good news, and even the playful, broken letters of DIRECT TO seem to hurry you along to the show.
